OP-SWU-001.text: After a non-power-on reset with invalid retained content, SWC-SUP-026 asks that entries which still pass an individual check stay readable for diagnosis. The retained-storage HAL here returns only a validity flag for the whole content, so the per-entry check, and the code used to record the loss (code 9 entity CONFIG chosen in DEC-SWU-004), are not decided.

OP-SWU-002.text: The inputs do not give how several reset flags set at once map to one cause, nor how the target's reset flags map to the abstract bits of hal_rcc.h; the port and the reference manual section and page (CON-SUP-002 names none) are needed. The priority IWDG, WWDG, POR, SW is a design choice (DEC-SWU-004).

OP-SWU-003.text: When start-up ends with a set latch or a fault, su_run returns HI_E_STATE and the idle behaviour of the start-up task (whether it services the independent watchdog while the diagnostic task runs, or lets the watchdog reset) is not stated by the architecture and is not coded in the units.

OP-SWU-004.text: OP-SWC-006 (reference manual section and page for GPIO access, atomicity of a pin write, pin state from reset to initialisation) is carried to the port: the units reach the pins only through hal_gpio.h and rely on neither property.

OP-SWU-005.text: Whether the execution time measured for the overrun decision includes preemption by higher-priority work (OP-SWC-016) is a requirement-level choice; the units measure wall-clock start to completion (DEC-SWU-006).

OP-SWU-009.text: A further detection of a coincident pass still performs the count, one hal_store_write and the report submission in fm_notify; the 5 us allocation of DEC-SWC-017 for a further decision depends on the execution time of hal_store_write and dc_submit_fault on the target, which the inputs do not give. OP-SWU-011.text: OP-SWC-012 (upstream, blocking) is unresolved: the core clock, the CRC throughput and the execution times are not given, so the execution-time, processor-time and simulator-integration assumptions (including DEC-SWU-003 chunk size and the 80 ms and 200 ms start-up wait figures) are not substantiated at design level.

OP-SWU-012.text: OP-SWC-013 (upstream, blocking) is unresolved: whether coincident detections with a report line in progress may exceed the 10 ms report deadline, or a started line may be abandoned, is a requirement-level choice. The 36-entry pending queue and its arrival argument (SWU-FLT-001) hold only within that choice; the lost-report counter records any report that does not fit.

OP-SWU-013.text: The linker script that places the read-only data of src/config_defaults.c inside __cfg_start..__cfg_end, and the build step that computes __cfg_crc over the block, are outside src/ and outside the inputs of this stage; the placement and the CRC value are to be confirmed at integration.

OP-SWU-014.text: Whether the target timer counter runs from the latest reset (value 0) and hal_timer_start leaves it running is a port fact not given by the inputs (OP-SWC-014 concerns the unit); ts_init relies on that contract (DEC-SWU-011). The reset-relative timestamp of SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003 cannot be stated correctly without this fact, so it blocks.
